steps.title: A More Equitable Bus Plan
steps.prompt: 다음 글의 중심 생각으로 가장 적절한 것은?
steps.passage: A city evaluated a proposed change to its local bus network. The plan would make popular routes more frequent, improving average waiting time across the city. Yet several neighborhoods with few passengers would lose their only direct connection to a hospital. At a public meeting, planners explained that maximizing the average benefit might overlook residents with limited travel choices. They compared alternative plans using both total passenger time and access to essential services. The final proposal kept some low-demand routes while improving busy corridors. It did not maximize a single numerical measure, but it served a broader public purpose. The planners noticed that the people most affected by a lost route were not always the people who attended public meetings. They consulted health centers and community organizations to learn how residents traveled for essential appointments. Some riders could transfer to another bus, but others faced long walks or additional fares. The city therefore examined the distribution of travel burdens rather than relying on one citywide average to summarize all experiences. Fairness in transport planning requires attention to the people behind the averages, especially those who have fewer alternatives.
choices: 버스 정책에서는 병원 접근성을 고려할 수 없다
교통 정책은 평균 성과와 이동 대안이 적은 주민의 접근성을 함께 고려해야 한다
평균 대기시간만 좋으면 모든 시민에게 이롭다
승객 수가 적은 지역은 필수 시설 접근성이 중요하지 않다
steps.explanation: 글의 논지를 요약하면 ‘교통 정책은 평균 성과와 이동 대안이 적은 주민의 접근성을 함께 고려해야 한다’이다. 근거: Fairness in transport planning requires attention to the people behind the averages, especially those who have fewer alternatives.
steps.evidenceQuote: Fairness in transport planning requires attention to the people behind the averages, especially those who have fewer alternatives.

steps.title: When One Rule Fits Nobody
steps.prompt: 다음 글의 중심 생각으로 가장 적절한 것은?
steps.passage: A school introduced the same daily reading target for every student. The rule was easy to explain, but teachers soon noticed problems. Confident readers finished quickly and became bored, while beginners struggled to understand short texts under the time limit. The school changed the program so that all students still practiced regularly but worked with different levels of difficulty. Teachers monitored both comprehension and participation, then adjusted targets as students improved. The revised program was harder to manage because it required more information and judgment. Nevertheless, it better matched the goal of helping each learner make progress. The school also avoided labeling students permanently as strong or weak readers. Teachers reassessed their needs regularly and allowed movement between levels. A student who struggled with science articles might understand historical stories very well, showing that ability could depend partly on the topic. The new system made space for both challenge and support. Flexibility required careful observation instead of simply lowering expectations for some students. A rule can be simple and consistent without being suitable for every person or situation.
choices: 개인별 목표를 설정하면 학습을 측정할 수 없다
쉬운 관리 방식이 항상 교육 효과도 가장 크다
동일한 규칙이 모든 학생에게 적합한 학습 조건은 아닐 수 있다
모든 학생의 실력은 동일하므로 과제도 같아야 한다
steps.explanation: 글의 논지를 요약하면 ‘동일한 규칙이 모든 학생에게 적합한 학습 조건은 아닐 수 있다’이다. 근거: A rule can be simple and consistent without being suitable for every person or situation.
steps.evidenceQuote: A rule can be simple and consistent without being suitable for every person or situation.
